text:
sam: heads-up, canary traffic for blue-release started spiking latency & 5xx after we flipped the experiment flag for adaptive batching. paging oncall.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: service/runtime latency p95 > 350ms for canary cluster (canary-3) — triggered at 09:13 UTC. Paging channel: incidents.
mira: oncall here — what's the scope? customer impact?
sam: quick numbers: canary-3 p50 110ms -> 180ms, p95 290ms -> 430ms, 5xx rate 1.1% -> 12% on canary. throughput down ~30%. noticing kernel fallback logs and batcher growth.
jordan: sounds like the new batching heuristic may be forming oversized batches and tripping a kernel path that falls back to a cheaper but slower execution. any logs?
sam: paste logs: ```
[2026-03-16T09:14:12Z] kernel_selector: WARN fallback to cpu_exec for model: rw-infer/gpt-8b q4 -> increased latency
[2026-03-16T09:14:17Z] batcher: INFO target_batch 64, inflight_queue 220, processing_time 320ms
[2026-03-16T09:14:22Z] runtime: ERROR exec_timeout shard=canary-3 request_id=...
```
blake: CS: two high-volume customers (chatflow-inc, notifyly) have thrown automated retries and some error alerts. reached out to account leads.
mira: can we flip the experiment flag (adaptive-batching) back as a kill-switch? where's the flag?
jordan: admin-console -> featureflags -> adaptive-batching-v2. quick curl to disable: ```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"flag":"adaptive-batching-v2","value":false}' https://admin.redwood/api/flags/toggle
```
mira: doing it now. will report once flipped.
ops-bot: request received: toggle adaptive-batching-v2 -> false (initiated by mira). Audit-id: au_9f7c
mira: flipped the flag at 09:16 UTC.
sam: after flip: canary-3 p95 dropping from 430ms -> 210ms within 40s, 5xx rate down to 2.3%. initial improvement visible.
incident-bot: Alert: latency p95 for canary-3 cleared at 09:17 UTC.
blake: CS update: informed Chatflow and Notifyly of temporary degraded responses, they saw retries but no long data loss. CS will prepare an incident note if we keep rollout paused.
jordan: recommend: immediate rollback of the release (we toggled flag, but release has other changes). propose rollback to previous deploy sha: deploy-2026-03-16-8f3b.
mira: agree. do rollback now through orchestrator. jordan, can you kick it? I'll start handoff to oncall-rotation for post-rollback monitoring.
jordan: running rollback: ```bash
redwoodctl rollout rollback --cluster canary --release deploy-2026-03-16-8f3b --yes
Rolling back canary-3... done.```

jordan: post-rollback checks: p95 stable 120-220ms, throughput back to normal. kernel_selector no longer emitting cpu_exec fallbacks.
mira: handing off to next oncall for 2h watch: @blake you take customer comm and watch alerts? i'll mark incident and add runbook tasks.
blake: taking it. will keep CS on standby, posting cust note draft in #customer-success and pinging account leads.
sam: for triage: root cause looks like batching heuristic misestimated sequence lengths, pushed batch sizes into a regime that triggered fallback kernels on the canary hardware profile. QA didn't hit same seq-length mix.
jordan: action items: 1) revert the rollout (done). 2) add a canary gating metric: kernel_fallback_rate < 0.5% before traffic ramp. 3) add runtime guard in batcher to cap batch size per model/hw pair. 4) run a synthetic workload that simulates high variance seq lengths for the next canary.
mira: I've created an internal incident ticket and assigned owners: triage doc -> INC-2026-0316-01, assignees jordan (runtime), sam (metrics/eval), blake (customer comms).
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0316-01 created by mira. Paging channel pinned.
blake: customer comm posted. awaiting any follow-ups.
jordan: suggest we also instrument kernel selector to emit a metric when path fallback occurs (already partially there but not alerted). will PR later today.
sam: will run a short eval harness to reproduce with the adaptive-batching heuristics disabled vs enabled, share results in the ticket.
mira: closing immediate paging. leave the rollout paused until we validate fixes and smaller canary traffic. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0316-01 status: mitigated. Next steps documented in ticket.
